name: PKINITtools - Get TGT from Certificate
description: Uses a PFX certificate (from ADCS relay or shadow credentials) to request a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT. Set KRB5CCNAME to the resulting ccache, then authenticate to services or run DCSync as the certificate's principal.

examples.label: Request a TGT from the PFX cert
Point Kerberos at the new ccache

notes:
Pass-the-Certificate: use a captured/forged cert (PKINIT) to request a TGT (gettgtpkinit/certipy) - cert-based auth survives password resets. Feeds into DCSync/PtT.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Dump domain hashes using the TGT.
On domain-joined Linux, reuse Kerberos credentials from ccache files (usually /tmp/krb5cc_*) or keytab files.
Rubeus handles Kerberos ticket abuse on Windows.

defense.why_it_works: A valid client-auth certificate is exchanged for a Kerberos TGT via PKINIT (Rubeus asktgt /certificate, gettgtpkinit) - authenticating as the certificate's identity without a password.
defense.prerequisites: A client-authentication certificate for the target principal (from ADCS abuse or theft).
defense.impact: A TGT as the certificate's principal (often a privileged user/DC) - password-independent domain access.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Certificate-based Kerberos auth (PKINIT): 4768 with a certificate; on the CA, 4886/4887 certificate requests where the SAN != requester; abnormal certificate issuance; ntlmrelay to ADCS shows a relayed request from a non-DC IP.
defense.artifacts: A PKINIT 4768 (certificate logon); the .pfx/TGT; Rubeus/gettgtpkinit execution.
defense.prevention: Harden ADCS templates (remove ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT, require manager approval, restrict enrollment); enforce HTTPS + Extended Protection on web enrollment (ESC8); monitor 4886/4887 and PKINIT logons; restrict who can enroll.
defense.evasion: Certificates are long-lived and reusable offline; PKINIT looks like smart-card logon, blending with legitimate certificate auth.
defense.misconfiguration: Pass-the-Certificate (PtC) attacks exploit ADCS certificate abuse (ESC1/ESC8) combined with Kerberos PKINIT. Shadow credentials (pywhisker) exploit write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to add a certificate-based authentication mechanism to any account. Pass-the-Ticket works because Kerberos tickets are extractable from LSASS memory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# msDS-KeyCredentialLink writable by attacker (GenericWrite on target account):
# pywhisker.py -t targetuser -a add
# Adds a fake device credential -> obtain certificate for targetuser
# -> PKINIT TGT as targetuser -> NTLM hash via UnPAC

# LSASS memory contains TGTs for all logged-in users:
# Mimikatz: sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Rubeus: dump /all
defense.secure_config:
# Prevent msDS-KeyCredentialLink abuse:
# Audit who has GenericWrite on privileged accounts
# Only SYSTEM/DCs should write msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity admin -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'Write'}

# Prevent ticket extraction:
# Enable Credential Guard (blocks LSASS memory reads)
# Protected Users group members: tickets not cached in LSASS

# ADCS: prevent ESC1/ESC8 (see those cards)
# Monitor: Event 4768 with certificate auth, Event 4769 unusual ticket lifetimes
